## Code and explanation share one clock {#code-steps data-step-summary="match"}

:::: {.two-col}
::: {}
```{.python .numberLines data-highlight="4" data-steps="1|2|3" data-step-indices="1|3|7" data-line-matches="1:observations|2:total|3:mean"}
observations = [2, 4, 6]
total = sum(observations)
mean = total / len(observations)
print(mean)
```
:::
::: {}
[Collect the observations.]{.fragment data-match="observations" data-fragment-index="1"}

[Compute their total.]{.fragment data-match="total" data-fragment-index="3"}

[Divide by the number of observations.]{.fragment data-match="mean" data-fragment-index="7"}
:::
::::

::: notes
Advance three times to teach, then once more for a color-matched overview. Previous restores the last highlight; earlier explanations remain visible.
:::

## Equations use the same clock {#equation-steps data-step-summary="match"}

:::: {.two-col}
::: {.equation-steps data-equation-steps="mean|total|count" data-step-indices="1|3|7"}
$$
\htmlClass{mean}{\bar{x}} = \frac{\htmlClass{total}{\sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i}}{\htmlClass{count}{n}}
$$
:::
::: {}
[The mean is the quantity we want.]{.fragment data-match="mean" data-fragment-index="1"}

[Add the observations in the numerator.]{.fragment data-match="total" data-fragment-index="3"}

[Divide by the number of observations.]{.fragment data-match="count" data-fragment-index="7"}
:::
::::

::: notes
Mean, total and count each have a matching explanation. The fourth advance restores all three terms to full strength. The classed terms are addressable after KaTeX typesetting. This cue also renders $\bar{x}=4$.
:::
